AND DwG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 36 s. 2021 Mar. 5, 2021 ATTY. JOHANNA MARIE B. BERMUDO Municipal Legal Officer Office of the Municipal Legal Officer Municipality of Barotac Nuevo, Iloilo Dear Atty. Bermudo: This has reference to your letter dated 15 July 2020 addressed to Engr. Ariel O. Iglesia, then Regional Director, DILG Region VI, requesting for this Department's opinion regarding the following: 1. Whether or not the public hearing conducted for the application of quarry permit was legitimate and proper; and 2. What are the essential requisites that the barangay must comply in order to have a valid public hearing? In an opinion rendered by DILG Region VII dated 17 August 2020, it was opined that pursuant to Department of Environment and Natural Resources Administrative order No. 2010-21 (DENR DAO No. 2010-21 public hearing is not explicitly required before a quarry permit may be issued. However, public hearing may be required by the Province to which the Municipality belongs. While we adhere to the aforementioned opinion, this Department deems it best to elaborate the foregoing. Foremost, although Republic Act No. 7942, otherwise known as the "Philippine Mining Act of 1995", did not specifically mention that a public hearing is necessary for applications for quarry permit, it is nonetheless imperative to note that for certain mining projects, an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) is required for an Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) to be issued, which is necessary for the issuance of a quarry permit. I Regional Legal Opinion No. 24, Series of 2020

In relation thereto, pursuant to DAO No. 2017-152, one (1) public hearing shall be conducted for projects requiring Environmental Impact Assessment (EIS), Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement (PEIS), Programmatic Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan (PERPMP) and EIS-based Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan (EPRMP). Further, item 2.1 , Annex A of DENR EMB MC 005, states that Mining and Quarrying Projects are required to have an ECC before the grant of quarry permit. Notices of the aforesaid hearing shall be posted in conspicuous places in the municipality and barangay where the project is proposed to be located at least 15 days prior to the scheduled hearing3. The EMB Office with jurisdiction over the processing of ECC application shall plan, initiate, and conduct the aforesaid hearing4. In the conduct thereof, efficient exchange of information and views between and among the project proponent, the EMB-DENR, relevant agencies, local government units (LGUs) and other stakeholders on the environmental impacts assessment, management and monitoring for proposed projects applying for an ECC shall be ensured5. Thus, while we adhere to the opinion rendered by the Regional Office, it is our considered view that if the application for quarry permit falls on item 2.1 , Annex A of DENR EMB MC 005, where an EIC and ECC are required to be secured for areas covering more than 25 hectares, public hearing is necessary. And such hearing shall be conducted by the EMB office. Therefore, the participation of the concerned barangay concerns solely on the exchange of views regarding the environmental impact of the project. Otherwise, if the area covers not more than 5 hectares, the application for quarry permit shall be applied before the Provincial Governor/City Mayor through the Provincial/City Mining Regulatory Board. To reiterate, there is no explicit provision of law which requires a public hearing in the barangay for purposes of acquiring a quarry permit. That being said, it is our considered view that there is no need for a barangay hearing to be conducted for the application of a quarry permit. However, if the area covered by the said application covers more than 25 hectares wherein an EIS and ECC are required, a public hearing is necessary which shall be conducted by the EMB office. On the other hand, if the area covers only not more than 5 hectares, the Provincial Government has the discretion whether or not a hearing shall be 2 02 May 2017 3 Item No. 12.4, 4 Item No. 13.2, 5 Item No. 13.3, DAO No. 2017-15 DAO No. 2017-15 DAO No. 2017-15

conducted6. Despite the foregoing, any opposition regarding the application for quarry permit shall be filed directly before the Regional Office concerned or through any PENRO or CENRO concerned for filing in the Regional Office for purposes of its resolution by the Panel of Arbitrators. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
